name: Dumbbell Biceps Curl
description: An isolation exercise emphasizing the elbow flexors, especially the biceps brachii.
instructions: Stand upright holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing forward.
Keep your elbows close to your sides.
Curl the weights toward your shoulders without swinging your upper arms.
Lower the dumbbells under control.

name: Hammer Curl
description: A curl variation using a neutral grip that trains the biceps and brachialis.
instructions: Stand with a dumbbell in each hand and palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows close to your torso.
Curl the dumbbells toward your shoulders while maintaining the neutral grip.
Lower the weights slowly.

name: Concentration Curl
description: A supported single-arm curl that limits body movement and emphasizes the biceps.
instructions: Sit with your legs apart and hold a dumbbell in one hand.
Brace the back of your upper arm against the inside of your thigh.
Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder.
Lower it slowly until your elbow is extended comfortably.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
description: A biceps curl performed on an incline bench with the arms positioned behind the torso.
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a moderate incline.
Sit back with a dumbbell in each hand and let your arms hang naturally.
Curl the dumbbells while keeping your upper arms relatively still.
Lower them under control.

name: EZ-Bar Curl
description: A barbell curl variation using an angled grip to train the elbow flexors.
instructions: Stand holding an EZ-bar with a comfortable underhand grip.
Keep your elbows near your sides.
Curl the bar toward your chest.
Lower it slowly without swinging.

name: Cable Biceps Curl
description: A cable-based curl that provides relatively consistent resistance through the movement.
instructions: Attach a straight or suitable handle to a low cable.
Stand upright and hold the handle with an underhand grip.
Curl the handle toward your shoulders.
Return to the starting position under control.

name: Triceps Pushdown
description: A cable exercise that primarily trains elbow extension through the triceps.
instructions: Stand facing a high cable attachment.
Hold the handle with your elbows close to your torso.
Push the handle downward until your elbows are comfortably extended.
Return slowly to the starting position.

name: Overhead Triceps Extension
description: An overhead elbow-extension exercise that trains the triceps through a long range of motion.
instructions: Hold one dumbbell with both hands above your head.
Keep your upper arms near your ears.
Bend your elbows to lower the weight behind your head.
Extend your elbows to raise the weight again.

name: Close-Grip Push-Up
description: A push-up variation that increases the contribution of the triceps while also training the chest and shoulders.
instructions: Start in a plank with your hands somewhat narrower than shoulder width.
Brace your trunk and lower your body with your elbows controlled.
Press through your hands to return to the starting position.
Keep your body aligned throughout the repetition.

name: Bench Dip
description: A bodyweight elbow-extension exercise emphasizing the triceps.
instructions: Place your hands on the edge of a stable bench behind you.
Position your feet comfortably in front of you.
Bend your elbows to lower your body a controlled distance.
Press through your hands to return upward.

name: Diamond Push-Up
description: A narrow-hand push-up that places substantial demand on the triceps.
instructions: Start in a plank with your hands close together beneath your chest.
Lower your body while keeping your trunk stable.
Press the floor away to extend your elbows.
Maintain controlled movement throughout.

name: Assisted Triceps Dip
description: A machine-assisted dip that allows the user to train the triceps with reduced bodyweight loading.
instructions: Set the assisted dip machine to an appropriate assistance level.
Grip the parallel handles and stabilize your shoulders.
Lower your body with controlled elbow flexion.
Press through the handles to return to the top.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
description: A vertical pressing movement that trains the deltoids and triceps.
instructions: Sit upright with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
Press the dumbbells upward without excessively arching your back.
Lower them under control to shoulder level.
Repeat smoothly.

name: Standing Barbell Overhead Press
description: A compound vertical press targeting the shoulders, triceps, and trunk stabilizers.
instructions: Hold the bar at upper-chest level with a comfortable overhand grip.
Brace your trunk and press the bar overhead.
Move your head slightly back as needed to clear the bar.
Lower the bar under control.

name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
description: An isolation movement emphasizing the middle deltoid.
instructions: Stand with light dumbbells at your sides.
Raise your arms outward in a controlled arc.
Stop around shoulder height or within a comfortable range.
Lower the weights slowly.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
description: A unilateral cable exercise emphasizing the middle deltoid.
instructions: Set a cable pulley near the bottom position.
Stand sideways to the machine and hold the handle with the far hand.
Raise the arm outward toward shoulder height.
Lower it slowly.

name: Front Dumbbell Raise
description: A shoulder-raising movement emphasizing the anterior deltoid.
instructions: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Raise one or both arms forward in a controlled motion.
Stop around shoulder height if comfortable.
Lower the weights slowly.

name: Reverse Dumbbell Fly
description: A rear-shoulder movement emphasizing the posterior deltoids and upper-back musculature.
instructions: Hinge forward with a neutral spine while holding dumbbells.
Let the weights hang beneath your chest.
Raise your arms outward while keeping the movement controlled.
Lower them slowly.

name: Face Pull
description: A cable pulling exercise that trains the rear deltoids and upper-back muscles.
instructions: Attach a rope to a cable at approximately upper-face height.
Pull the rope toward your face while separating your hands.
Keep your shoulders controlled rather than shrugging.
Return the rope slowly.

name: Arnold Press
description: A dumbbell shoulder press incorporating rotation during the pressing movement.
instructions: Start seated with dumbbells in front of your shoulders and palms facing you.
Rotate your palms outward while pressing overhead.
Lower the dumbbells while reversing the rotation.
Use controlled movement throughout.

name: Landmine Press
description: An angled pressing movement that trains the shoulders, triceps, and upper chest.
instructions: Hold the end of a secured barbell near shoulder height.
Brace your trunk and press the bar upward and forward.
Keep the movement controlled.
Return the bar toward your shoulder.

name: Cable Y-Raise
description: A light-resistance shoulder movement emphasizing upward-rotating shoulder musculature.
instructions: Use two low cable handles or suitable cable attachments.
Raise your arms diagonally upward into a Y shape.
Keep the motion smooth and avoid shrugging excessively.
Lower your arms slowly.

name: Dumbbell Scaption
description: A shoulder elevation movement performed in the scapular plane.
instructions: Hold light dumbbells with your palms facing inward.
Raise your arms slightly forward from your sides.
Lift them within a comfortable range.
Lower them slowly.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
description: A machine-based vertical press that trains the deltoids and triceps.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles begin around shoulder level.
Grip the handles and brace your trunk.
Press upward without locking the elbows aggressively.
Return the handles under control.

name: Push-Up
description: A foundational bodyweight pressing exercise emphasizing the chest, triceps, and anterior shoulders.
instructions: Start in a plank position with your hands approximately shoulder-width apart.
Lower your body while maintaining a stable trunk.
Press the floor away to return to the starting position.
Use a controlled range of motion.

name: Incline Push-Up
description: A modified push-up using an elevated surface to reduce loading while training the chest.
instructions: Place your hands on a stable elevated surface.
Walk your feet back into a straight-body position.
Lower your chest toward the surface.
Press back to the starting position.

name: Decline Push-Up
description: A push-up with elevated feet that increases the relative loading of the upper body.
instructions: Place your feet on a stable elevated surface.
Position your hands on the floor.
Lower your chest toward the floor while maintaining alignment.
Press back up.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
description: A horizontal pressing movement emphasizing the pectoral muscles.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding dumbbells near your chest.
Press the dumbbells upward while maintaining stable shoulders.
Lower them under control toward the sides of your chest.
Repeat smoothly.

name: Barbell Bench Press
description: A compound horizontal press that strongly trains the pectorals and also involves the triceps and shoulders.
instructions: Lie on a bench with the bar positioned above your chest.
Grip the bar securely and unrack it with appropriate assistance when needed.
Lower it toward the mid-chest under control.
Press it upward without losing shoulder or trunk stability.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
description: An incline pressing movement emphasizing the clavicular portion of the pectoralis major.
instructions: Set a bench to a moderate incline.
Hold dumbbells near the upper chest.
Press them upward while keeping your shoulders controlled.
Lower them slowly.

name: Cable Chest Fly
description: A cable fly that trains horizontal shoulder adduction with emphasis on the chest.
instructions: Set two cable handles around chest height.
Stand between the cables with a slight bend in your elbows.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest.
Return slowly while maintaining control.

name: Dumbbell Chest Fly
description: A fly movement emphasizing the pectoral muscles through horizontal shoulder adduction.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench with dumbbells held above your chest.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the weights outward in a controlled arc.
Bring them back together above your chest.

name: Chest Press Machine
description: A machine-based horizontal press that trains the chest and triceps.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles align approximately with mid-chest.
Grip the handles and stabilize your shoulders.
Press the handles forward.
Return them slowly.

name: Low-Incline Push-Up
description: A slightly elevated push-up variation suitable for building pressing strength.
instructions: Place your hands on a low stable platform.
Keep your body in a straight line.
Lower your chest toward the platform.
Press back up.

name: Pec Deck Fly
description: A machine fly that emphasizes the pectoral muscles.
instructions: Adjust the machine so your elbows or hands align comfortably with your chest.
Brace your trunk and grip the pads or handles.
Bring the arms together in front of you.
Return slowly to the starting position.

name: Kneeling Push-Up
description: A modified push-up that reduces the amount of bodyweight supported by the upper body.
instructions: Place your hands beneath your shoulders and knees on the floor.
Keep your torso aligned from your knees through your head.
Lower your chest toward the floor.
Press back up.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
description: A hip-extension exercise strongly emphasizing the gluteus maximus. The movement is suitable for all genders; programming can be individualized by training goal rather than sex.
instructions: Position your upper back against a stable bench and place a padded barbell across your hips.
Plant your feet and brace your trunk.
Drive through your feet to extend your hips.
Pause briefly near the top and lower under control.

name: Glute Bridge
description: A bodyweight hip-extension exercise that trains the gluteus maximus.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet planted.
Brace your trunk.
Drive through your feet to lift your hips.
Lower your hips slowly.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
description: A unilateral bridge variation that challenges hip extension and pelvic control.
instructions: Lie on your back with one foot planted and the other leg extended.
Brace your trunk and press through the planted foot.
Lift your hips while keeping your pelvis controlled.
Lower slowly and repeat.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A unilateral squat variation that trains the glutes and quadriceps while challenging balance.
instructions: Place the top of one foot on a stable bench behind you.
Position the other foot far enough forward for a comfortable range.
Lower your body by bending the front knee and hip.
Drive through the front foot to stand.

name: Romanian Deadlift
description: A hip-hinge movement emphasizing the glutes and hamstrings.
instructions: Hold a barbell or dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Push your hips backward while keeping your spine neutral.
Lower the weights along your legs until you feel an appropriate stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
description: A hip-extension exercise emphasizing the gluteus maximus.
instructions: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable.
Brace yourself against the machine.
Extend the working leg backward without twisting your pelvis.
Return the leg slowly.

name: Quadruped Hip Extension
description: A bodyweight hip-extension movement emphasizing the gluteus maximus.
instructions: Start on your hands and knees.
Brace your trunk and keep your pelvis stable.
Drive one foot upward and backward without arching excessively.
Lower the leg with control.

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
description: A hip-abduction exercise emphasizing the gluteus medius and other lateral hip muscles.
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs extended.
Keep your pelvis stacked and stable.
Raise the upper leg without rotating your toes upward.
Lower it slowly.

name: Banded Lateral Walk
description: A resisted lateral movement that trains the hip abductors, including the gluteus medius.
instructions: Place a resistance band around your thighs or lower legs as appropriate.
Adopt a comfortable athletic stance.
Step sideways while maintaining band tension.
Continue in both directions with controlled steps.

name: Step-Up
description: A unilateral step exercise that trains the glutes and quadriceps.
instructions: Stand facing a stable step or platform.
Place one foot fully on the platform.
Drive through that foot to step upward.
Lower yourself under control.

name: Reverse Lunge
description: A unilateral leg exercise involving the glutes, quadriceps, and hamstrings.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet comfortable apart.
Step one foot backward.
Lower your body while bending both knees.
Push through the front foot to return to standing.

name: Frog Pump
description: A bodyweight hip-extension variation that emphasizes the gluteal muscles.
instructions: Lie on your back and bring the soles of your feet together.
Allow your knees to open comfortably.
Drive through your feet to lift your hips.
Lower your hips under control.

name: Bodyweight Squat
description: A fundamental lower-body movement training the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings.
instructions: Stand with your feet at a comfortable width.
Bend your hips and knees to lower your body.
Keep your feet planted and your trunk controlled.
Push through your feet to stand.

name: Goblet Squat
description: A squat variation using a dumbbell or kettlebell held near the chest.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell close to your chest.
Squat down while keeping your feet planted.
Maintain a controlled torso position.
Drive through the floor to stand.

name: Barbell Back Squat
description: A loaded squat that trains the quadriceps, glutes, and other lower-body muscles.
instructions: Position a properly loaded barbell securely across your upper back.
Brace your trunk and squat by bending the hips and knees.
Keep the bar controlled over your base of support.
Drive through your feet to return to standing.

name: Front Squat
description: A barbell squat variation that places the load in front of the body and strongly challenges the quadriceps and trunk.
instructions: Position the bar securely across the front of your shoulders.
Brace your trunk and descend into a squat.
Keep your elbows appropriately elevated for your grip.
Drive upward through your feet.

name: Leg Press
description: A machine-based compound exercise training the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings.
instructions: Position your feet securely on the platform.
Release the safety mechanism according to the machine instructions.
Lower the platform under control.
Press through your feet to return without forcefully locking your knees.

name: Leg Extension
description: An isolation exercise emphasizing the quadriceps.
instructions: Adjust the machine so the knee joint aligns appropriately with its pivot.
Place your lower legs against the pad.
Extend your knees smoothly.
Lower the weight under control.

name: Lying Leg Curl
description: An isolation movement emphasizing the hamstrings.
instructions: Lie face down on the machine and position your ankles beneath the pads.
Keep your hips stable against the pad.
Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Lower the weight slowly.

name: Seated Leg Curl
description: A seated machine exercise emphasizing the hamstrings.
instructions: Adjust the seat and thigh pad securely.
Position your lower legs against the roller.
Bend your knees to pull the roller downward and backward.
Return the weight slowly.

name: Standing Calf Raise
description: A calf exercise emphasizing the gastrocnemius and soleus through plantarflexion.
instructions: Stand with the balls of your feet supported and your heels free.
Rise onto your toes as high as comfortable.
Pause briefly near the top.
Lower your heels slowly.

name: Seated Calf Raise
description: A seated plantarflexion exercise that emphasizes the soleus.
instructions: Sit with the balls of your feet supported and your knees bent.
Raise your heels by pressing through the balls of your feet.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower your heels slowly.

name: Walking Lunge
description: A dynamic unilateral lower-body exercise training the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings.
instructions: Stand tall and step forward with one leg.
Lower your body until both knees are comfortably bent.
Push through the front foot to step forward.
Alternate legs as you move.

name: Romanian Deadlift
description: A hip-hinge exercise primarily training the hamstrings and glutes.
instructions: Hold the weights in front of your thighs.
Push your hips backward while maintaining a neutral spine.
Lower the weights until an appropriate hamstring stretch is felt.
Drive the hips forward to stand.

name: Dead Bug
description: A core-stability exercise emphasizing trunk control while the limbs move.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hips and knees bent.
Brace your abdominal muscles while maintaining a controlled spine position.
Slowly extend the opposite arm and leg.
Return them and alternate sides.

name: Bird Dog
description: A quadruped stability exercise training the trunk and hip musculature.
instructions: Start on your hands and knees.
Brace your trunk and extend one arm and the opposite leg.
Keep your pelvis relatively level.
Return slowly and switch sides.

name: Plank
description: An isometric trunk exercise that trains the abdominal and spinal stabilizing muscles.
instructions: Support yourself on your forearms and toes.
Brace your trunk and keep your body aligned.
Breathe normally while maintaining the position.
Stop when you can no longer maintain good form.

name: Side Plank
description: An isometric exercise emphasizing the lateral trunk muscles and obliques.
instructions: Lie on your side and support your body on one forearm.
Stack or stagger your feet for balance.
Lift your hips until your body forms a straight line.
Hold while maintaining controlled breathing.

name: Reverse Crunch
description: A trunk-flexion exercise that emphasizes the abdominal musculature.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent.
Brace your abdomen and bring your knees toward your torso.
Curl your pelvis gently upward without swinging.
Lower your hips slowly.

name: Bicycle Crunch
description: A dynamic abdominal exercise involving trunk rotation and flexion.
instructions: Lie on your back with your hands lightly supporting your head.
Lift your legs and bend your knees.
Rotate your trunk as one knee moves toward the opposite elbow.
Alternate sides with controlled movement.

name: Mountain Climber
description: A dynamic plank exercise that challenges the abdominal muscles while also involving the hips and shoulders.
instructions: Start in a stable high-plank position.
Drive one knee toward your chest.
Return the foot and alternate legs.
Keep your trunk controlled rather than bouncing.

name: Hollow Body Hold
description: An advanced isometric trunk exercise requiring strong abdominal bracing.
instructions: Lie on your back and brace your abdomen.
Lift your shoulders and legs slightly from the floor.
Keep your lower back controlled against the floor.
Hold for the prescribed duration.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
description: A demanding anti-extension core exercise requiring strong trunk control.
instructions: Kneel with the ab wheel under your shoulders.
Brace your trunk before moving.
Roll forward only as far as you can maintain control.
Pull the wheel back by engaging your trunk and hips.

name: Pallof Press
description: An anti-rotation exercise that trains the trunk's ability to resist rotational forces.
instructions: Stand sideways to a cable or resistance band anchor.
Hold the handle at your chest.
Brace your trunk and press your hands forward.
Resist the pull trying to rotate your torso.

name: Forearm Plank Knee Tap
description: A plank variation that challenges abdominal bracing and pelvic control.
instructions: Start in a forearm plank.
Brace your trunk and lower one knee toward the floor.
Return the leg without shifting your torso excessively.
Alternate sides.

name: Suitcase Carry
description: A loaded carry that challenges lateral trunk stability and grip.
instructions: Hold one weight at your side.
Stand tall with your shoulders level.
Brace your trunk and walk under control.
Switch sides and repeat.

name: Wrist Curl
description: A wrist-flexion exercise emphasizing the forearm flexor muscles.
instructions: Sit and rest your forearms on your thighs or a bench.
Hold light dumbbells with your palms facing upward.
Curl your wrists upward.
Lower the weights slowly.

name: Reverse Wrist Curl
description: A wrist-extension exercise emphasizing the forearm extensor muscles.
instructions: Rest your forearms securely on your thighs or a bench.
Hold light weights with your palms facing downward.
Extend your wrists upward.
Lower the weights under control.

name: Farmer's Carry
description: A loaded carry that strongly challenges grip and forearm endurance.
instructions: Hold a weight in each hand.
Stand tall with your shoulders controlled.
Walk with steady, deliberate steps.
Set the weights down safely after the desired distance.

name: Plate Pinch Hold
description: A grip exercise emphasizing the thumb and finger muscles of the hand and forearm.
instructions: Hold a suitable weight plate between your thumb and fingers.
Stand upright while keeping the wrist neutral.
Hold for the prescribed duration.
Lower the plate carefully.

name: Dead Hang
description: An isometric hanging exercise that challenges grip and forearm endurance.
instructions: Grip a secure pull-up bar.
Hang with your body controlled and shoulders comfortable.
Maintain the grip for the desired duration.
Release carefully when finished.

name: Towel Hang
description: A hanging grip variation that challenges the hands and forearms.
instructions: Secure a strong towel over a suitable pull-up bar.
Grip the towel firmly with both hands.
Hang while maintaining controlled shoulders.
Release carefully when your grip begins to fatigue.

name: Wrist Roller
description: A forearm endurance exercise involving repeated wrist flexion and extension.
instructions: Hold the wrist-roller handle at approximately chest height.
Rotate the handle to wind the attached weight upward.
Continue with controlled wrist movements.
Reverse the direction to lower the weight.

name: Hammer Curl Hold
description: An isometric neutral-grip hold that challenges the forearm and elbow-flexor musculature.
instructions: Hold dumbbells with your palms facing each other.
Bend your elbows to approximately 90 degrees.
Maintain the position without swinging.
Lower the weights carefully.

name: Reverse Curl
description: A pronated curl that trains the brachioradialis and forearm extensor musculature.
instructions: Hold a barbell or EZ-bar with an overhand grip.
Keep your elbows near your sides.
Curl the bar upward.
Lower it slowly.

name: Cable Wrist Flexion
description: A cable-based wrist-flexion movement for the forearm flexors.
instructions: Attach a low cable to a suitable handle.
Rest your forearm securely while keeping your wrist free to move.
Flex your wrist toward your palm.
Return slowly.

name: Cable Wrist Extension
description: A cable-based wrist-extension movement for the forearm extensors.
instructions: Secure a low cable attachment and position your forearm.
Keep the forearm stable.
Extend your wrist upward.
Return slowly.

name: Rice Bucket Hand Drill
description: A low-load grip and hand-conditioning drill using resistance from dry rice.
instructions: Place your hands into a clean container of dry rice.
Open and close your hands against the rice resistance.
Move your wrists and fingers through controlled directions.
Stop if you experience pain or excessive fatigue.

name: Lat Pulldown
description: A vertical pulling exercise emphasizing the latissimus dorsi and upper-back musculature.
instructions: Sit at the pulldown station and secure your thighs under the pads.
Grip the bar comfortably wider than shoulder width.
Pull the bar toward your upper chest while keeping your torso controlled.
Return the bar slowly.

name: Pull-Up
description: A bodyweight vertical pull that strongly trains the latissimus dorsi and elbow flexors.
instructions: Grip a secure pull-up bar with an overhand grip.
Brace your trunk and pull your body upward.
Move until your chin reaches the bar or an appropriate range.
Lower yourself under control.

name: Assisted Pull-Up
description: A machine-assisted vertical pull that allows progressive practice of the pull-up pattern.
instructions: Set the machine to an appropriate assistance level.
Grip the handles securely.
Pull your body upward while keeping your trunk controlled.
Lower under control.

name: Seated Cable Row
description: A horizontal pulling movement training the middle back, latissimus dorsi, and elbow flexors.
instructions: Sit with your feet supported and hold the cable handle.
Brace your trunk and maintain a controlled torso.
Pull the handle toward your torso.
Extend your arms slowly to return.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
description: A unilateral rowing movement emphasizing the latissimus dorsi and upper back.
instructions: Support one hand and knee on a stable bench.
Hold the dumbbell with the opposite hand.
Pull the weight toward your torso while keeping your shoulder controlled.
Lower it slowly.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
description: A supported row that trains the upper and middle back while reducing the need for trunk stabilization.
instructions: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with dumbbells in your hands.
Allow your arms to hang beneath you.
Pull the dumbbells toward your torso.
Lower them slowly.

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
description: A compound horizontal pulling movement training the lats, rhomboids, trapezius, and other back muscles.
instructions: Hold the barbell and hinge forward with a neutral spine.
Brace your trunk and keep the bar close to your body.
Pull the bar toward your lower chest or upper abdomen.
Lower it under control.

name: Inverted Row
description: A bodyweight horizontal pulling exercise that trains the upper back and elbow flexors.
instructions: Set a secure horizontal bar at an appropriate height.
Hang beneath it with your body straight.
Pull your chest toward the bar.
Lower yourself under control.

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
description: A cable exercise emphasizing shoulder extension and the latissimus dorsi.
instructions: Attach a straight bar or rope to a high cable.
Stand facing the machine with arms extended.
Pull the attachment downward toward your thighs while keeping the elbows mostly straight.
Return slowly.

name: Back Extension
description: A hip-extension movement involving the spinal erectors, glutes, and hamstrings.
instructions: Position yourself securely on a back-extension bench.
Brace your trunk and hinge at the hips.
Extend your hips until your torso returns to a neutral position.
Avoid excessive spinal hyperextension.

name: Dumbbell Pullover
description: A shoulder-extension movement involving the latissimus dorsi and chest.
instructions: Lie across or along a stable bench while holding one dumbbell above your chest.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head through a comfortable range.
Keep your trunk controlled.
Pull the dumbbell back above your chest.

name: Scapular Pull-Up
description: A controlled hanging exercise focusing on scapular movement and upper-back musculature.
instructions: Hang from a secure pull-up bar.
Keep your elbows mostly straight.
Depress and retract your shoulder blades to raise your body slightly.
Relax the shoulder blades in a controlled manner.

name: Chin Tuck
description: A gentle neck exercise that trains cervical positioning. It is not a proven method for selectively removing facial fat or changing facial structure.
instructions: Sit or stand tall with your head facing forward.
Gently draw your chin backward as though making a small double-chin motion.
Hold briefly without looking downward.
Relax and repeat.

name: Neck Rotation
description: A gentle cervical mobility exercise. It supports neck movement rather than directly reshaping facial features.
instructions: Sit or stand upright.
Slowly rotate your head toward one side.
Return to the center.
Repeat toward the opposite side without forcing the range.

name: Neck Side Bend
description: A gentle neck mobility exercise for the muscles along the sides of the neck.
instructions: Sit or stand tall.
Slowly tilt one ear toward the same-side shoulder.
Return to the center without rotating your head.
Repeat on the other side.

name: Neck Flexion and Extension
description: A gentle cervical mobility sequence. It should be performed within a comfortable range rather than forced.
instructions: Sit or stand with your spine upright.
Slowly nod your head forward within a comfortable range.
Return to neutral and gently look upward without forcing the motion.
Return to neutral between repetitions.

name: Lip Press
description: A gentle facial-muscle exercise involving controlled lip compression. It should not be presented as a proven facial-sculpting method.
instructions: Sit comfortably with your jaw relaxed.
Gently press your lips together.
Hold the contraction briefly without clenching your teeth.
Relax completely.

name: Cheek Puff
description: A gentle facial-muscle coordination exercise involving the cheeks.
instructions: Relax your jaw and lips.
Gently fill your cheeks with air.
Hold briefly while keeping the jaw relaxed.
Release the air slowly.

name: Alternating Cheek Puff
description: A facial coordination drill involving controlled movement of air between the cheeks.
instructions: Fill your mouth gently with air.
Move the air into one cheek.
Transfer it slowly to the opposite cheek.
Keep your jaw relaxed throughout.

name: Gentle Smile Hold
description: A controlled facial-expression exercise involving the muscles around the mouth and cheeks.
instructions: Relax your jaw and forehead.
Make a comfortable natural smile.
Hold briefly without straining.
Relax fully before repeating.

name: Eyebrow Raise
description: A facial-expression movement involving the muscles that elevate the eyebrows.
instructions: Relax your face.
Raise both eyebrows gently.
Hold briefly without wrinkling or straining excessively.
Relax and repeat.

name: Gentle Eye Squeeze
description: A light facial-muscle coordination exercise around the eyes. It is not intended to change eye shape.
instructions: Relax your forehead and jaw.
Gently close your eyes without squeezing forcefully.
Hold briefly.
Open your eyes and relax.

name: Tongue-to-Palate Rest Position
description: A gentle oral-posture practice emphasizing relaxed tongue placement and nasal breathing when comfortable. It should not be marketed as a guaranteed facial-reshaping technique.
instructions: Rest the tongue gently against the palate without force.
Keep the lips comfortably closed if nasal breathing is easy.
Keep the teeth relaxed rather than clenched.
Maintain normal, comfortable breathing.

name: Jaw Relaxation Drill
description: A relaxation exercise intended to reduce unnecessary jaw tension rather than increase jaw muscle size.
instructions: Sit upright and let your shoulders relax.
Allow your jaw to hang comfortably with the teeth slightly separated.
Breathe slowly and avoid clenching.
Maintain the relaxed position for several breaths.

name: Gentle Jaw Opening
description: A gentle mandibular mobility exercise. It is not a proven method for reshaping the jawline.
instructions: Sit upright with your jaw relaxed.
Slowly open your mouth within a comfortable range.
Pause briefly without forcing the opening.
Close your mouth gently.

name: Controlled Jaw Lateral Movement
description: A gentle mandibular mobility drill involving side-to-side jaw movement.
instructions: Keep your head still and shoulders relaxed.
Move your lower jaw slightly toward one side.
Return to the center.
Repeat toward the other side without forcing the range.

name: Controlled Jaw Protraction
description: A gentle mandibular movement that trains controlled jaw positioning rather than attempting to change bone structure.
instructions: Start with your jaw in a relaxed neutral position.
Move the lower jaw slightly forward.
Hold briefly without clenching.
Return to neutral.

name: Jaw Isometric Opening
description: A very gentle isometric jaw exercise. Excessive resistance or pain should be avoided because the jaw joint can be irritated by overloading.
instructions: Place a clean fingertip or hand lightly beneath your chin.
Attempt to open your mouth gently while providing only minimal resistance.
Hold briefly without pain or tooth clenching.
Relax completely.

name: Jaw Isometric Closing
description: A light isometric exercise involving the jaw-closing muscles. It should be performed without forceful clenching.
instructions: Keep your jaw in a neutral position.
Place two fingers lightly against the underside of the chin.
Gently attempt to close the jaw against minimal resistance.
Relax immediately after the brief contraction.

name: Masseter Relaxation
description: A relaxation drill for the masseter muscles. Relaxation is generally more appropriate than aggressive jaw loading for people prone to jaw tension.
instructions: Place your fingertips gently over the cheek area where the masseter can be felt.
Keep your teeth slightly separated.
Breathe slowly while consciously relaxing the muscle.
Avoid forceful massage or pressing on painful areas.

name: Gentle Masseter Isometric
description: A low-intensity isometric contraction of the jaw-closing muscles. There is no established need to train masseter size for a healthy jaw.
instructions: Keep your head and neck neutral.
Bring your teeth together only very lightly.
Hold the contraction briefly.
Release completely and keep the jaw relaxed.

name: Tongue-to-Palate Jaw Relaxation
description: A relaxed oral-posture drill that avoids forceful jaw clenching and is not a guaranteed jawline-shaping method.
instructions: Place the tongue gently against the roof of the mouth.
Keep the teeth separated or only lightly touching without clenching.
Relax the jaw muscles.
Breathe normally.

name: Chin Tuck with Jaw Relaxation
description: A posture-oriented movement combining gentle cervical retraction with relaxed jaw positioning.
instructions: Sit or stand tall.
Gently draw your chin backward without looking downward.
Keep your teeth relaxed and avoid jaw clenching.
Return to neutral.

name: Slow Controlled Chewing Motion
description: A gentle jaw-movement drill that mimics chewing without requiring hard or prolonged resistance. It is not intended to enlarge the masseters.
instructions: Keep your posture upright and jaw relaxed.
Perform small, slow chewing-like movements.
Avoid hard clenching or excessive repetition.
Stop if the jaw becomes painful, clicks painfully, or feels fatigued.

name: Jaw Opening with Tongue Rest
description: A gentle jaw-mobility exercise emphasizing controlled opening while keeping the tongue and jaw relaxed.
instructions: Rest your tongue comfortably against the roof of your mouth.
Slowly open your jaw within a pain-free range.
Pause briefly.
Close gently and return to a relaxed position.

name: Jaw Mobility Sequence
description: A gentle sequence combining opening, closing, and small lateral jaw movements. It is intended for mobility and control rather than facial reshaping.
instructions: Begin with the jaw relaxed.
Open and close the mouth slowly within a comfortable range.
Perform small controlled side-to-side movements.
Finish with the jaw relaxed and teeth unclenched.
